previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF ~20%), diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath with sudden onset orthopnea. Evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism, acute aortic pathology, and myocardial infarction. Imaging showed pulmonary edema superimposed on emphysematous changes and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. The patient was treated with IV and oral diuretics, optimized on beta-blocker therapy, and educated on fluid and sodium restriction. Acute kidney injury developed, likely due to contrast and diuresis, prompting temporary discontinuation of lisinopril and metformin. Symptoms improved, and he was discharged home with services, stable on room air, with follow-up planned for renal function and consideration of a sleep study for suspected obstructive sleep apnea.

Brief Hospital Course:

failure - Treated with Lasix IV boluses on admission followed by 
the previously prescribed maintenance dose of Lasix 40 mg po 
daily. Continued beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor. Demonstrated 
adequate room air oxygenation prior to discharge.

# Chest pain - No ischemic EKG changes. Serial cardiac 
biomarkers were negative. Exercise stress MIBI showed no anginal 
type symptoms or significant EKG changes, no focal myocardial 
perfusion defect, but an increase in left ventricular 
dilatation, with worsening of global hypokinesis, and decreased 
LVEF from 36% to 27% compared with ___ exam. Continued 
aspirin, BB, ACE-I, statin. Smoking cessation counseling was 
provided. An outpatient cardiology follow up appointment was 
scheduled. 

# History of VT s/p ICD placement - EKG and telemetry showed 
ventricular ectopy with bigeminy/trigeminy which was 
asymptomatic and well-tolerated hemodynamically. Electrolytes 
were within normal limits. Continued metoprolol and amiodarone.

# Chronic kidney disease stage III - Creatinine remained stable 
despite diuresis. Restarted lisinopril.

# Diabetes type II - Sugars were well-controlled on an insulin 
sliding scale. Restarted metformin prior to discharge.

# Hypertension - Blood pressure was well-controlled on 
metoprolol and lisinopril.

# Dyslipidemia - Continued simvastatin and niacin.
